title: Attenuated warmup for regional fallthrough and SLO guard
author: Nora Patel
description: Motivation: During a recent regional failover we observed abrupt traffic cutovers causing cold KV/cache churn and immediate SLO pressure on the hot region; this led to cascading circuit flips and tenant-visible errors. This change introduces an "attenuated warmup" path for regional fallthrough: when a region is marked as failing/evacuating, the router can opt-in to a gradual handoff that ramps token budgets, warms prefix/KV caches opportunistically, and applies an SLO guard window to avoid immediate full-throughput reroutes. Summary of changes: 1) routing/controller: add WarmupState machine with three phases (sample, ramp, normal) and per-region warmup timers; 2) slo-enforcer: plumb warmup coefficients into budget calculation so SLO-based throttles are relaxed according to ramp schedule but still bounded by tenant SLA; 3) cache-warming: introduce non-blocking async prefetch hooks on routed fallthrough requests to populate KV and prefix caches without stalling the request path; 4) telemetry: new metrics (region_warmup_phase, warmup_allowed_tokens, warmup_cache_prefetch_rate) and detailed auditing for decisions; 5) ops: config knobs and rollout flags (warmup.enabled, warmup.default_window_ms, warmup.initial_fraction) with sensible defaults. Implementation notes: The warmup approach is intentionally conservative: initial_fraction defaults to 0.05 (5% of steady-state token allowance) for the first window_ms (default 15s), then exponentiates towards 1.0 over the configured window with jitter to avoid herd effects. Token allowances are applied at the router token-bucket layer and are additive with existing tenant quotas; this avoids bypassing tenant limits. Cache prefetches are rate-limited and use a bounded worker pool to protect hotspots. The change also adds an operator-visible endpoint to kick a region into warmup manually for postmortem-driven recovery. Backwards compatibility: All warmup behavior is feature-flagged off by default for non-enterprise clusters and scoped to release channels. The router falls back to existing immediate-failover path if warmup is disabled or if the receiving region reports insufficient capacity. Testing and validation: - Unit tests for WarmupState transitions and token math. - Integration tests simulating region drain with synthetic traffic, asserting no spike in 95/99 latency and no increase in error-rate above configured thresholds. - Perf bench (perf-canary) simulating 50k qps burst with warmup enabled showed 0.6x drop in cold-start errors vs immediate failover and a 12% transient increase in median latency during ramp windows (acceptable per SRE policy). - Canary rollout plan described in Ops notes below. Related work: Linear ENG-19345 (regional-fallthrough-warmup) and ENG-19702 (slo-enforcer-budgets). Also references incident notes INC-2026-02-11 where abrupt failover caused regression. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration canaries green - [x] Telemetry metrics added and dashboards drafted - [x] Ops runbook and rollback included - [x] Feature-flag and defaults set to safe values Rollout plan: 1) Enable warmup in preprod and staged perf-canary at 10% of traffic for 24h. 2) Monitor new metrics and 95/99 latency, token drop rate, and cache-prefetch success. 3) Gradually increase traffic to 100% in target region across 48h if no regressions. 4) If SLO regressions occur, operator can toggle warmup.enabled off or reduce warmup.initial_fraction. Rollback: immediate toggle of warmup.enabled to false reverts behavior; warmup state is ephemeral and does not change persisted tenant quotas. Observability: dashboards added in observability-pack with alerts on warmup_failed_prefetch_rate > 1% and region_warmup_phase stuck > 120s. Security and safety: no new privileged data paths added; prefetches respect tenant data access controls and are performed with the same request-scoped principals. Review thread and conversation summary: - Ethan Kline: asked for stronger guardrails around tenant opt-outs; we added tenant opt-out via attribute warmup.allow_opt_out=false and documented in README. - Maya Ruiz: requested a stricter upper-bound on aggregate warmup tokens to avoid overall capacity blowouts; we added a per-region aggregate cap and unit tests. - Samir Ghosh: flagged potential double-counting with existing autoscaler signals; added a regression in autoscaler integration test and a short-circuit that prefers autoscaler capacity hints. Merge notes: CI passed after two reruns of flaky e2e; perf-canary results attached. Merged using squash-and-merge. Reasons this PR is different: rather than an immediate circuit/fallback flip, this introduces a controlled ramp with cache-warm strategies and SLO-aware token math to reduce cascading failures during regional handoffs.

release_notes: Add attenuated regional warmup to smooth failovers: controlled ramping of token budgets, async cache prefetching, and SLO-aware guard windows. Feature-flagged and opt-out capable for tenants. Improves cold-start error rate during regional failovers.
review_thread:
Ethan Kline (reviewer): Please add tenant opt-out and ensure warmup can't bypass tenant quotas.
Author (Nora): Added warmup.allow_opt_out and enforced tenant quota additive behavior. Added unit tests.

Maya Ruiz (reviewer): Need aggregate cap per-region to avoid unexpected capacity consumption.
Author: Added region_warmup_aggregate_cap and tests to validate caps under synthetic burst.

Samir Ghosh (reviewer): Potential interaction with autoscaler signals—can we respect autoscaler hints?
Author: Autoscaler hint short-circuit added; warmup reduces allowance if autoscaler reports low headroom. Integrated into integration tests.
